title: Which fish are lowest in mercury?

seo.title: Fish lowest in mercury: practical choices
seo.meta_description: Sardines, salmon, shrimp, clams, and many other small or shorter-lived seafood species tend to be low in mercury. Species matters far more than whether the fish is fresh, frozen, or canned.
seo.search_intent: Find lower-mercury seafood choices and understand why mercury levels differ so much among species.

excerpt: FDA monitoring data place scallops at 0.003 ppm mean mercury, clams and shrimp at 0.009 ppm, and sardines at 0.013 ppm. Choosing species from FDA/EPA's Best Choices list is a practical way to keep mercury exposure low while still eating seafood.
content_html:
You do not have to avoid seafood to reduce mercury exposure. Species choice can change the amount dramatically. Smaller, shorter-lived fish and shellfish generally accumulate less methylmercury than large predatory fish that feed higher in the food chain for many years.

Some of the lowest averages in FDA monitoring data

FDA's commercial seafood monitoring table reports mean mercury concentrations in parts per million (ppm). These are averages across sampled products, so an individual fish can vary.

SeafoodMean mercury
Scallop0.003 ppm
Clam0.009 ppm
Shrimp0.009 ppm
Oyster0.012 ppm
Sardine0.013 ppm
Tilapia0.013 ppm
Canned salmon0.014 ppm
Anchovy0.016 ppm

The size of the gap matters. Sardines average 0.013 ppm in this dataset, while swordfish is around 1 ppm—roughly 70 to 80 times the mean concentration. That is why a blanket statement about “mercury in fish” misses the most useful information.

How FDA and EPA turn the numbers into choices

The FDA/EPA fish-advice chart places many familiar foods in its Best Choices category, including anchovies, Atlantic mackerel, canned light tuna, cod, salmon, sardines, shrimp, tilapia, trout, and several shellfish. For people who are pregnant or breastfeeding, the agencies recommend 2–3 servings, totaling 8–12 ounces per week, from lower-mercury choices.

Fresh versus frozen is not the main mercury question

Mercury is accumulated by the animal before harvest; freezing and normal cooking do not meaningfully remove it. Canned products also differ mainly because of species. FDA monitoring lists canned light tuna at 0.126 ppm mean mercury versus 0.014 ppm for canned salmon.

A simple shopping rule

Rotate among lower-mercury species instead of relying on one fish every week. Small oily fish such as sardines and anchovies, salmon, shrimp and other shellfish, and many white fish make that easy while preserving the nutritional benefits of seafood.

faq.question: Are sardines low in mercury?
faq.answer: Yes. FDA monitoring data list sardines at a mean of 0.013 ppm, among the lower values for commercial seafood.

faq.question: Does cooking fish remove mercury?
faq.answer: Not to a meaningful degree. Species and the amount eaten are much more important for exposure.

faq.question: Is canned light tuna a low-mercury choice?
faq.answer: FDA/EPA place canned light tuna in Best Choices, although its monitored mean of 0.126 ppm is higher than sardines at 0.013 ppm or canned salmon at 0.014 ppm.
